clue.text: Many under canvas make a pile

indicators.note: being under canvas means staying in the tent, so the letter goes inside the camp

parts.note: canvas stands for tents, hence a camp
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of campers sleeping in tents together build up a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a stacked heap, of bricks for firing or of potatoes stored under earth.

clue.text: Student circle in Sicilian city or part of Spain

indicators.note: in places the student and circle inside the city name

parts.note: Catania is a city on the east coast of Sicily
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A student ring in Sicily or a region in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is a region in north-eastern Spain, capital Barcelona.

clue.text: Battlefield anecdotes about sappers

indicators.note: about means going around, so the anecdotes surround the engineers

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: War stories about military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a scene of conflict or contest.

clue.text: Share it with 17's leader, this suite of pieces

indicators.note: with here joins the further letter on to the end of the share and it

parts.note: part means a share

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the answer at 17 across

parts.note: the answer to 17 across

explanation.surface: A musical suite divided up with a reference to another clue's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a Baroque instrumental suite, as by Bach.

clue.text: American politician eager, we hear, to be a popular leader

parts.note: DEM is short for a Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: agog means keenly eager

explanation.surface: An American politician keen to become a leader of the people.
explanation.walkthrough: AGOG said aloud is spelt AGOGUE here, as in synagogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a rabble-rouser who wins the masses by appeals to emotion.

clue.text: Intend to make a sketch

definitions.meaning: to plan or mean to do something
to draw up a plan or drawing

explanation.surface: Planning to draw something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to purpose something, and to draft a drawing.

clue.text: Brawny copper in terrible slum, all right initially

indicators.note: in means the metal symbol goes within the scrambled slum
terrible signals that the word slum is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of all and right

explanation.surface: A tough policeman in a dreadful slum where all seems fine at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes MUSL from SLUM; CU goes 'in' it, then A and R from 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular means strong and well-built.

clue.text: Thought likely to be Roman dug up outside

indicators.note: outside means the reversed dug wraps around the Latin word
up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: esse is Latin for to be

explanation.surface: Probably a Roman artefact, unearthed outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DUG into GUD, which goes 'outside' ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guessed means supposed or reckoned probable.

clue.text: Sort of gold tiara for an old swordsman

indicators.note: sort of hints at a version of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of golden headdress for an ancient fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator fought with a sword in Roman arenas.

clue.text: Thrashed, beheaded and devoured

indicators.note: beheaded removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: beaten means thrashed

explanation.surface: Someone was flogged, decapitated and consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten means consumed, swallowed.

clue.text: Speculators rebuilt this store

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Investors have redeveloped this shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns the nine letters of THIS STORE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorists are people who form hypotheses, i.e. who speculate.

clue.text: Girl has little weight to make a law

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a small unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A slim young woman decides to pass legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to pass a measure into statute.

clue.text: "We'll make Smith principal first violin, shall we?"

definitions.text: "We'll make Smith principal first violin, shall we?"

parts.words: "We'll make Smith principal first violin, shall we?"
parts.note: the first violin is the orchestra's leader, so this asks whether Smith should be put in charge, a query that also nudges toward the desired yes

explanation.surface: A conductor proposes promoting a player called Smith to lead the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A query phrased so as to prompt the reply wanted; here also literally about appointing the orchestral leader.

clue.text: Divine drink 10 mixed? Right

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the earlier answer are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 10 across

explanation.surface: A heavenly cocktail is shaken up and declared correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the beverage of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Tom goes to a company doctor's burial-place

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree, with the 's

explanation.surface: A man named Tom joins a firm's physician at a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground tunnels used for interring the dead.

clue.text: Judicial commands also accepted by ships' officers

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: mates are officers on merchant ships
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Court orders are likewise received by the officers aboard ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandates are official orders, as from a court to a lower body.

clue.text: Ayesha OK'd him for change in Arab leadership

parts.note: Ayesha is the immortal queen of Rider Haggard's novel She

indicators.note: for change means the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A woman approved a man for a shift of power in an Arab state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha is 'She-who-must-be-obeyed' of H. Rider Haggard's novel; 'for change' turns OKDHIM into IKHDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikhdom is the rule or territory of an Arab chief.

clue.text: Column finally accepted by the more devout?

indicators.note: accepted by means held inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, so piër jokingly means more pious; the question mark flags it
last means finally

explanation.surface: A newspaper column at last welcomed by the more religious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' is architectural, not a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall.

clue.text: Such verisimilitude given to Pooh-Bah's narrative?

definitions.text: Such verisimilitude given to Pooh-Bah's narrative?

parts.words: Such verisimilitude given to Pooh-Bah's narrative?
parts.note: in The Mikado, Pooh-Bah offers corroborative detail to lend a certain kind of verisimilitude to an otherwise bald and unconvincing narrative

explanation.surface: A question about how realistic a pompous official's story sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh-Bah is the Lord High Everything Else in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado; the clue quotes his famous line.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line speaks of 'artistic verisimilitude', i.e. realism added for creative effect.

clue.text: Marine mammal to observe, say? Neat

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken and another spelt

parts.note: see means observe
neat is an old word for cattle, so a calf

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to watch a sea creature, called neat.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea calf is an old name for the common seal.

clue.text: Direction to clean up the plant

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
to purge is to cleanse or rid of impurities

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and tidy the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' pretends to be a factory; it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is a weed of the Euphorbia genus with milky sap.

clue.text: Soft part of plant for a cat

parts.note: p is piano, soft in music
the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a stamen

explanation.surface: A gentle piece of greenery for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard.

clue.text: This head a nominal leader may be Arabic

definitions.meaning: add head to this word to get a leader in name only
a numeral such as 1, 2, 3 in the Arabic system

explanation.surface: A puppet ruler who might come from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is a leader without real power; and a digit, as in Arabic numerals.

clue.text: It's dashed dotty to follow "the strange device, Excelsior' or this!

definitions.text: It's dashed dotty to follow "the strange device, Excelsior' or this!

parts.words: It's dashed dotty to follow "the strange device, Excelsior' or this!
parts.note: Longfellow's poem Excelsior has a banner with 'the strange device, Excelsior!' and the punctuation there is a stroke above a dot, i.e. dashed and dotty

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that it is crazy to copy Longfellow's banner motto.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol after Excelsior (and after 'this') is a vertical dash over a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol placed after a cry or exclamation is a line over a dot.

clue.text: Work unit to reverse plant disease

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work or energy

indicators.note: reverse means the short word to is turned backwards

explanation.surface: A unit of labour sets out to undo a crop blight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease of rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Write a poem for this conductor

parts.note: a is written as an before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A request to compose verses for the orchestra's maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is a positive electrode, conducting current into a device.

clue.text: Organ-stop is one removed from W African country

indicators.note: removed from signals that a letter is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: The Gambia is a small country in West Africa
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An organ part has been taken away from a West African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamba is an organ register imitating the viola da gamba's string tone.

clue.text: It's useful as tinder, barring ill luck

definitions.meaning: rotten, dry wood that catches easily and is used to start fires
the phrase said to ward off misfortune, like knocking on wood

explanation.surface: Something that helps light a fire, provided nothing goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk wood used as kindling; and the superstitious phrase to avert bad fortune.

clue.text: Sort of square, to request church working-party

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's tool
ask for means request
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A drawing tool is used to petition the church for a team of volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a unit assembled for a specific job.

clue.text: Scope, say, for obtaining discharge

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken and another spelt

parts.note: room means scope, space to act

explanation.surface: An instrument such as a telescope used to obtain something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus flowing from the eyes or nose.
